Apply **BODMAS**: solve the **bracket** (29 + 19 = 48) and **multiply** (48 × 2 = 96).

The expression becomes: 76 + 85 − 49 + 96 − 91.

Combine all **positive terms** (76 + 85 + 96 = 257) and **negative terms** (49 + 91 = 140).

Final result: 257 − 140 = 117.

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 76 + 85 − 49 + (29 + 19) × 2 − 91

**Method Used:** **BODMAS Rule** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ 76 + 85 − 49 + (48) × 2 − 91 (Solving **Bracket**)

⇒ 76 + 85 − 49 + 96 − 91 (Performing **Multiplication**)

⇒ 161 − 49 + 96 − 91 (Performing **Addition** from left)

⇒ 112 + 96 − 91 (Performing **Subtraction**)

⇒ 208 − 91 (Performing **Addition**)

⇒ 117 (Final **Subtraction**)

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It is an acronym used to remember the **order of operations** in mathematics: **Brackets** (), **Of** (or Orders like roots/powers), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Grouping Positive and Negative Terms

To minimize calculation errors, sum all **positive numbers** and all **negative numbers** separately, then find their difference at the final step.

questions.question: 92 - 36 + 28 ÷ 4 + (19 of 2) - 14 + 17 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **BODMAS** rule to solve the expression in order: **Brackets**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Solve **Of**: (19 of 2) = 19 × 2 = 38.

Solve **Division**: 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

Simplify remaining terms: 92 − 36 + 7 + 38 − 14 + 17 = 104.

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 92 − 36 + 28 ÷ 4 + (19 of 2) − 14 + 17

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS Rule**

⇒ 92 − 36 + 28 ÷ 4 + 38 − 14 + 17 (Solving **Of** first)

⇒ 92 − 36 + 7 + 38 − 14 + 17 (Solving **Division**)

⇒ (92 + 7 + 38 + 17) − (36 + 14) (Grouping **Addition** and **Subtraction** terms)

⇒ 154 − 50

⇒ 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Defines the order of operations: **Brackets** (round, curly, square), **Of** (powers/multiplication), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

The 'Of' Operator

The word **'of'** functions as multiplication but must be performed before regular **division** and **multiplication** in the BODMAS hierarchy.

Grouping Strategy

For faster **simplification**, group all positive terms together and all negative terms together before the final subtraction.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Count the **decimal places** in both numbers: 0.36 has 2 places and 0.00036 has 5 places.

Subtract the decimal places: 5 − 2 = 3 places **difference**.

Since the **divisor** has more decimal places, the result is 10³.

Result = 1000.

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 0.36 ÷ 0.00036

**Method:** Convert **decimal numbers** into **fractions** for easier calculation.

⇒ 0.36 = 36/100

⇒ 0.00036 = 36/100000

⇒ Expression = (36/100) ÷ (36/100000)

⇒ Expression = (36/100) × (100000/36)

⇒ Expression = 100000 ÷ 100

⇒ 1000

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Division of Decimals

When dividing by a **decimal**, move the decimal point in the **divisor** to the right until it becomes a **whole number**, and move it the same number of places in the **dividend**.

Power of 10 Rule

Multiplying a decimal by 10ⁿ shifts the **decimal point** n places to the **right**, while dividing by 10ⁿ shifts it n places to the **left**.

BODMAS Rule

In multi-step **simplification** questions, always follow the order of **Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction**.

questions.question: (10)³ + (6)³ + 3 × 10 × 6 × 16 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given expression is in the form of the **algebraic identity** a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b) = (a + b)³.

Here, let **a = 10** and **b = 6**, which implies **(a + b) = 16**.

Substituting these values, the expression simplifies to **(10 + 6)³**.

⇒ **16³ = 4096**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4096.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (10)³ + (6)³ + 3 × 10 × 6 × 16

**Method:** Step-by-step simplification using **arithmetic powers** and **BODMAS**.

⇒ Calculate the cubes: 10³ = **1000** and 6³ = **216**.

⇒ Calculate the product: 3 × 10 × 6 × 16 = 180 × 16.

⇒ 180 × 16 = **2880**.

⇒ Total Sum = 1000 + 216 + 2880.

⇒ Total Sum = **4096**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4096.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Cube Identities

The formula for the **cube of a sum** is (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b). Similarly, the **cube of a difference** is (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b).

Sum and Difference of Cubes

Do not confuse (a+b)³ with **a³ + b³**. The latter factors as (a + b)(a² − ab + b²), while **a³ − b³** factors as (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Standard Cube Values

For faster calculations in **competitive exams**, it is recommended to memorize cubes up to 20, such as **11³ = 1331**, **12³ = 1728**, and **16³ = 4096**.

questions.question: The area of a rhombus is 54 square cm. One of the diagonal is 9 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the other diagonal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area of Rhombus** = (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 2

Product of **Diagonals** = 2 × Area = 2 × 54 = 108

Other Diagonal = 108 ÷ 9 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the **rhombus** = 54 cm²

Length of one **diagonal** (d₁) = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of a rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa93776287f80f35d84c02428d57b9f0d4e721453401bf1a47eef65d7e155557.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 54 = (1/2) × 9 × d₂

⇒ 54 × 2 = 9 × d₂

⇒ 108 = 9 × d₂

⇒ d₂ = 108 ÷ 9

⇒ d₂ = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All sides of a **rhombus** are equal, and the diagonals bisect each other at **right angles** (90°).

Side and Diagonals Relationship

The side 'a' of a rhombus can be found using the formula: 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Perimeter of Rhombus

The perimeter is given by 4 × side. For this rhombus, side = √(4.5² + 6²) = 7.5 cm, so **Perimeter** = 30 cm.

questions.question: Sum of the diagonals of a rhombus is 14 cm. Area of this rhombus is 24 square cm. What is the side (in cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of diagonals (d₁ + d₂) = 14 and Product (d₁d₂) = 2 × Area = 48.

By inspection, the numbers summing to 14 and multiplying to 48 are 6 and 8.

Half-diagonals are 3 and 4.

In a rhombus, side (s) forms a right-angled triangle with half-diagonals: s = √(3² + 4²).

Using the 3-4-5 **Pythagorean triplet**, side = 5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

questions.question: Least Common Multiple of A and B is 40 and C = 18. What is the Least Common Multiple of A, B and C?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ To find the **LCM** of (40, 18), check the multiples of the larger number **40**. Multiples of 40: 40, 80, 120, 160, 200, 240, 280, 320, **360**. Check divisibility by **18**: 360 ÷ 18 = 20 (Perfectly divisible). The first common multiple for both is **360**. **∴ The correct answer is 360.**

questions.question: The Highest Common Factor of two numbers is 15 and their Least Common Multiple is 360. What is the product of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The fundamental property of two numbers states: **Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM**.

Product = 15 × 360

Product = 5400

**∴ The correct answer is 5400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Highest Common Factor (HCF)** = 15

**Least Common Multiple (LCM)** = 360

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0acea6dc24c3a90f9e6dbb0186095c1aa54ddbfff9e36a928f6cbc7b699261a9.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Product of numbers (n₁ × n₂) = HCF(n₁, n₂) × LCM(n₁, n₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Product = 15 × 360

⇒ Product = 15 × (300 + 60)

⇒ Product = (15 × 300) + (15 × 60)

⇒ Product = 4500 + 900

⇒ Product = 5400

**∴ The correct answer is 5400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators). LCM = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are **co-prime**, their **HCF** is always 1, and their **LCM** is equal to their product.

HCF/LCM Relationship

The **LCM** of any set of numbers is always exactly divisible by their **HCF**.

questions.question: A is 50 percent less than B. B is how much percentage more than A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **A** is **R% less** than **B**, then **B** is more than **A** by:

**[R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100**

Given **R = 50**

⇒ [50 ÷ (100 − 50)] × 100 = [50 ÷ 50] × 100 = 100%

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**A** is **50% less** than **B**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a622a093b231c05c9f025e4512d66591ca0291f1375b64be81b5111ab7966efe.png] 

Let the value of **B** be 100.

⇒ **A** = 100 − 50% of 100

⇒ **A** = 100 − 50 = 50

Now, we need to find how much **percentage more** **B** is compared to **A**.

⇒ Difference = **B − A** = 100 − 50 = 50

⇒ **Percentage More** = [Difference ÷ A] × 100

⇒ [50 ÷ 50] × 100

⇒ 1 × 100 = 100%

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

Percentage Increase = [(New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100.

Reciprocal Relation

If A is 1/x less than B, then B is 1/(x−1) more than A. Here, 50% = 1/2, so B is 1/(2−1) = 1/1 = 100% more than A.

Base Change Property

Percentage values change based on the **denominator (base)**. When comparing B to A, A becomes the base.

questions.question: Selling price and cost price of an article is Rs. 550 and Rs. 500 respectively. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Ratio of **Cost Price** (CP) to **Selling Price** (SP) = 500 : 550 = 10 : 11. Profit = 11 − 10 = 1 unit. **Profit percentage** = (Profit units ÷ CP units) × 100. **Profit percentage** = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%. **∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

questions.question: If 25 percent of 500 is 25 percent more than A, then what is the value of A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Value = 25% of 500 = 125.

Since 125 is 25% **more than** A, it represents 125% of A.

125% → 125

100% (Value of A) → (125 ÷ 125) × 100 = 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage value = 25% of 500

Relation: This value is 25% **greater than** A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7b37617e6c8bc8ad095c235e7a4039c9ee760c75dedb73c6a9620801fdaa1a2f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Number = Base × (1 + Percentage Increase/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 25% × 500 = (25/100) × 500 = 125

⇒ 125 = A + (25/100) × A

⇒ 125 = A + 0.25A

⇒ 125 = 1.25A

⇒ A = 125 ÷ 1.25

⇒ A = 12500 ÷ 125

⇒ A = 100

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

To increase a quantity by x%, multiply it by (1 + x/100). For example, a 25% increase is equivalent to multiplying by 1.25 or 5/4.

Fractional Equivalents

Knowing common fractions like 25% = 1/4 or 20% = 1/5 helps in faster calculation. Here, A + A/4 = 5A/4 = 125.

Base Value Concept

Always identify the **base** (100%) on which the percentage is calculated. In this problem, A is the base value.

questions.question: A person has a loss of 30 percent on selling price. What will be his loss percentage on the cost price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 units.

**Loss** = 30% of SP = 30 units.

**Cost Price (CP)** = SP + Loss = 100 + 30 = 130 units.

**Actual Loss%** (on CP) = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (30 ÷ 130) × 100.

Loss% = 300 ÷ 13 ≈ 23.08%.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.08 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Loss percentage** on **Selling Price** = 30%

**Formula Used:**

1. **Cost Price (CP)** = **Selling Price (SP)** + **Loss**

2. **Loss percentage on CP** = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d705164b0e2a419e8a7a43cc8bc0110c03a21c2ab1a05176a0273ca455360669.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Selling Price (SP)** be ₹100.

⇒ **Loss** = 30% of ₹100 = ₹30.

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = SP + Loss = 100 + 30 = ₹130.

⇒ **Loss Percentage on CP** = (30 ÷ 130) × 100.

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = 300 ÷ 13 = 23.0769...

⇒ **Loss Percentage** ≈ 23.08%.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.08 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit/Loss on Selling Price

When profit or loss is calculated on **Selling Price**, it is called the **apparent profit/loss**. To find the **actual profit/loss**, it must always be calculated on the **Cost Price**.

Conversion Formulas

If **Loss% on SP** is L%, then **Loss% on CP** = [L ÷ (100 + L)] × 100. If **Profit% on SP** is P%, then **Profit% on CP** = [P ÷ (100 − P)] × 100.

Basic P&L Relations

**Profit** = SP − CP (when SP > CP). **Loss** = CP − SP (when CP > SP). In case of loss, CP is always greater than SP.

questions.question: A, B and C working alone can complete a work in 18, 27 and 36 days respectively. In how many days A, B and C together can complete 2/3 part of the same work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Work** = LCM(18, 27, 36) = 108 units

Individual **Efficiencies**: A = 6, B = 4, C = 3

**Total Efficiency** (A + B + C) = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13 units/day

**Work to complete** = 2/3 × 108 = 72 units

**∴ The correct answer is 72/13 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** alone = 18 days

Time taken by **B** alone = 27 days

Time taken by **C** alone = 36 days

**Formula Used:**

**Total Work** = Efficiency × Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **A**
 18
 108 (LCM of 18, 27, 36)
 6
 
 

 **B**
 27
 4
 
 

 **C**
 36
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Combined efficiency** of **A, B and C** = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13 units/day

⇒ **2/3 part** of the work = 2/3 × 108 = 72 units

⇒ **Time taken** to complete 72 units = Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ **Required Time** = 72 ÷ 13 days

**∴ The correct answer is 72/13 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Work and Efficiency Relationship**

The time taken to complete a work is **inversely proportional** to the efficiency of the person (Time ∝ 1/Efficiency).

**Combined Work Formula**

If A and B can do a work in x and y days respectively, together they can do it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

**Work and Wages**

When workers work for the same duration, their **wages** are distributed in the **ratio of their efficiencies**.

questions.question: A and B undertook a work for Rs. 4200. A alone can do that work in 21 days. B alone can do the same work in 28 days. They started and completed the work together. What will be the difference in the amounts (in Rs.) they will receive?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Efficiency ratio** of A and B is the inverse of their **time ratio** = 28 : 21 = 4 : 3.

The total **wage** of ₹4200 is divided into 4 + 3 = 7 parts based on **efficiency**.

Value of 1 part = 4200 ÷ 7 = ₹600.

The **difference** between their shares is (4 − 3) = 1 part.

Difference in amount = 1 × 600 = ₹600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A can complete work in 21 days, B in 28 days. Total contract amount = ₹4200.

**Formula Used:** Wages are distributed in the ratio of **efficiency** when the duration of work is the same for all individuals.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 21

 B

⇒ Total **Efficiency** parts = 4 + 3 = 7 units

⇒ Total amount for 7 units = ₹4200

⇒ Amount for 1 efficiency unit = 4200 ÷ 7 = ₹600

⇒ Share of A = 4 × 600 = ₹2400

⇒ Share of B = 3 × 600 = ₹1800

⇒ Difference in amounts = 2400 − 1800 = ₹600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Wages and Efficiency

Wages are directly proportional to the amount of work done. If time is constant, **Wage Ratio = Efficiency Ratio**.

Work-Time Relation

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to **Time** taken to complete a task (Efficiency = 1 ÷ Time).

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to **Time and Work**, filling efficiency is treated as positive work and leakage/emptying efficiency is treated as negative work.

questions.question: A man walking at the speed of 8 km/hr covers a certain distance in 4 hours and 30 minutes. If he covers the same distance by cycle in 4 hours, then what is the speed (in km/hr) of cycle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time** (Speed ∝ 1/Time).

Ratio of **Time** (Walk : Cycle) = 4.5 hr : 4 hr = 9 : 8

Ratio of **Speed** (Walk : Cycle) = 8 : 9

Since **Walking Speed** 8 units = 8 km/hr, then 9 units = 9 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Walking Speed** (S₁) = 8 km/hr

**Time taken** (T₁) = 4 hr 30 min = 4.5 hr

**Time taken by Cycle** (T₂) = 4 hr

**Formula Used:**

**Distance** = **Speed** × **Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a364f5efffa35002758b5d14e5ed005ec142f42b71dbfbba44b23acc0756078.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total **Distance** = S₁ × T₁

⇒ **Distance** = 8 × 4.5 = 36 km

⇒ **Speed of Cycle** (S₂) = **Distance** ÷ T₂

⇒ S₂ = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Distance Property

When distance is fixed, the ratio of speeds is the inverse of the ratio of time taken: S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert **minutes** into **hours**, divide by 60 (e.g., 30 min = 30/60 = 0.5 hr). To convert **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18.

Average Speed

If equal distances are covered at speeds 'u' and 'v', then **Average Speed** = 2uv ÷ (u + v).

questions.question: A train having length 150 metres takes 8 seconds to cross a 250 metres long bridge. How much time (in seconds) will this train take to cross a 500 metres long bridge?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Since the **speed of the train** remains constant, the **time** taken is directly proportional to the **total distance** covered. Total Distance 1 = 150 + 250 = 400 m Total Distance 2 = 150 + 500 = 650 m Ratio of Distances = 400 : 650 = 8 : 13 Since 8 units = 8 seconds, then 13 units = 13 seconds. **∴ The correct answer is 13 sec.**

questions.question: An article is sold for 30 percent loss. The value of discount given is equal to the (7/10) of the selling price. Cost price of the article is what percent of its marked price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100. **Loss** = 30% ⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 70.

**Discount** = 7/10 of **SP** = 0.7 × 70 = 49.

**Marked Price (MP)** = **SP** + **Discount** = 70 + 49 = 119.

Required percentage = (**CP** / **MP**) × 100 = (100 / 119) × 100 ≈ 84.03%.

**∴ The correct answer is 84.03%.**

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 30 percent and 20 percent are given on an article. If the marked price of the article is Rs. 500, then what is the value of net discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Discount %** = x + y − (xy/100)

Effective Discount % = 30 + 20 − (30 × 20 / 100) = 50 − 6 = 44%

**Net Discount** = 44% of **Marked Price**

Net Discount = 44% of ₹500 = (44/100) × 500 = ₹220

**∴ The correct answer is ₹220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹500, Successive discounts = 30% and 20%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e1f528bfc66cbe01b21a2784a7ad85016598fd04d388d255a81d8505b0cbc4d.png] 

⇒ First discount = 30% of ₹500 = (30/100) × 500 = ₹150

⇒ Value after first discount = 500 − 150 = ₹350

⇒ Second discount = 20% of ₹350 = (20/100) × 350 = ₹70

⇒ Total **Net Discount** = First discount + Second discount = 150 + 70 = ₹220

⇒ Alternatively, Final **Selling Price (SP)** = 350 − 70 = ₹280

⇒ Net Discount = **Marked Price (MP)** − Selling Price (SP) = 500 − 280 = ₹220

**∴ The correct answer is ₹220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For three successive discounts of a%, b%, and c%, calculate the equivalent for the first two, then use that result with the third.

Selling Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) ... × (1 − dₙ/100).

Net Discount Value

Net Discount = Marked Price − Final Selling Price.

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 10 percent and 30 percent are given on an article. What is the net discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Discount = [a + b − (a × b / 100)]%

Here, a = 10% and b = 30%

Net Discount = [10 + 30 − (10 × 30 / 100)]%

Net Discount = [40 − 3]% = 37%

**∴ The correct answer is 37%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given values: First discount = 10%, Second discount = 30%

Assume the **Marked Price (MP)** of the article is 100 units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24339619f179d1586ce430c1a031562232a89c9718f5f127a0823c42bf721384.png] 

⇒ First discount = 10% of 100 = 10 units

⇒ Price after first discount = 100 − 10 = 90 units

⇒ Second discount = 30% of 90 = 27 units

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 90 − 27 = 63 units

⇒ **Total Discount** = 100 − 63 = 37 units

⇒ **Net Discount %** = (37 / 100) × 100 = 37%

**∴ The correct answer is 37%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts Formula

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the single equivalent discount = [x + y − (xy / 100)]%.

Fraction Method

Final Price = Marked Price × (100−d₁)/100 × (100−d₂)/100. This is useful for complex percentages.

Successive Percentage Change

For successive increases of x% and y%, the net change = [x + y + (xy / 100)]%. Note the change in sign compared to discounts.
